extracted.intended_audience: prospective authors preparing manuscripts for Acta Mathematica Hungarica (Springer Nature)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and requirements for preparing and submitting manuscripts (research and non-research articles) to Acta Mathematica Hungarica, including formatting, ethical, data, artwork, and authorship standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / simultaneous_submission prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a manuscript implies that the work described has not been published before; that it is not under consideration for publication anywhere else; that its publication has been approved by all co-authors and by the responsible authorities at the institute where the work has been carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher will not be held legally responsible for claims. The manuscript should not be submitted to more than one journal for simultaneous consideration. Concurrent or secondary publication is sometimes justifiable only under certain conditions (e.g., translations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for previously published material
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors wishing to include figures, tables, or text passages that have already been published elsewhere are required to obtain permission from the copyright owner(s) for both the print and online format and to include evidence that such permission has been granted when submitting their papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any material received without such evidence will be assumed to originate from the authors. Some publishers do not grant electronic rights for free; Springer will not refund permission costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide editable source files on submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should preferably be submitted in the original file format and authors must provide all relevant editable source files at every submission and revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to submit source files might cause unnecessary delays in review and production. Include the original source (including all style files and figures) and a PDF of the compiled output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The title page must contain: title (concise and informative); author names; affiliations (institution, department, city, state, country); a clear indication and active e-mail of the corresponding author; if available, 16-digit ORCID of the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If address information is provided with affiliation it will be published. For temporarily unaffiliated authors, only city and country of residence are captured (not e-mail) unless requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large Language Models (LLMs) and authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Language Models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, do not currently satisfy authorship criteria and cannot be attributed authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of an LLM should be properly documented in the Methods section (or suitable alternative). AI-assisted copy editing does not need to be declared (defined as readability/style/grammar fixes), but there must be human accountability for the final text. Check Springer guidance on generative AI images where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an abstract of 150 to 250 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract should not contain any undefined abbreviations or unspecified references. (Additional trial-registration items apply for life-sciences journals when relevant.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide 4 to 6 keywords for indexing purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keywords support indexing and discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements and Declarations required
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a 'Statements and Declarations' section in the manuscript containing relevant declarations (e.g., Competing Interests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that do not include relevant declarations will be returned as incomplete. See specific sections for sample wording and required items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Springer Nature LaTeX template and [iicol] option
rubrics_metrics.description: For LaTeX submissions authors are encouraged to use the Springer Nature LaTeX template and to choose the formatting option '[iicol]'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should include original source, style files, figures, and a PDF. Authors preparing manuscripts in LaTeX can use the bibliography style file sn-basic.bst included in the template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings decimal system and depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the decimal system of headings with no more than three levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent hierarchical structure for headings throughout the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations should be defined at first mention and used consistently thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid undefined abbreviations in abstracts and throughout the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes can be used to give additional information, including citation of a reference included in the reference list, but should not consist solely of a reference citation and should never include bibliographic details of a reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes to the text are numbered consecutively; footnotes to tables use superscript lower-case letters (or asterisks for significance). Footnotes to the title or authors are not given reference symbols. Always use footnotes instead of endnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments placement and funder naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgments of people, grants, funds, etc. should be placed in a separate section on the title page; names of funding organizations should be written in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear acknowledgment and funding statements on the title page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference citation style in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference citations in the text should be identified by numbers in square brackets (e.g., [3], [1-3, 7]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite references using the journal's numeric-square-bracket style consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference list contents and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of references should include only works cited in the text and that have been published or accepted for publication; entries should be numbered consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal communications and unpublished works should be mentioned only in the text, not in the reference list. If available, always include DOIs as full DOI links in the reference list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal name abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the standard abbreviation of a journal’s name according to the ISSN List of Title Word Abbreviations (LTWA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure, use the full journal title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table numbering and citation
rubrics_metrics.description: All tables are to be numbered using Arabic numerals and should always be cited in text in consecutive numerical order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each table supply a caption explaining the components; identify previously published material with a reference at the end of the caption. Footnotes to tables should be indicated by superscript lower-case letters or asterisks and included beneath the table body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic figure submission and file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply all figures electronically and indicate what graphics program was used to create the artwork. Preferred formats: vector graphics – EPS; halftones – TIFF; MSOffice files are also acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vector graphics containing fonts must have fonts embedded. Name figure files with 'Fig' and the figure number (e.g., Fig1.eps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Line art technical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Line art (black and white graphic with no shading) should not use faint lines/lettering; all lines must be legible with minimum width 0.1 mm (0.3 pt); scanned line drawings/bitmap line drawings should have at least 1200 dpi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vector graphics containing fonts must have fonts embedded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halftone art resolution and magnification
rubrics_metrics.description: Halftone art (photographs, drawings with shading) should have a minimum resolution of 300 dpi. If any magnification is used indicate it by scale bars within the figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure photographic/halftone clarity at final size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination artwork resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Combination artwork (halftone + line art, extensive lettering, color diagrams) should have a minimum resolution of 600 dpi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare combination images at adequate resolution to preserve both halftone and line elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color art submission and print considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Color art is free of charge for online publication. If black-and-white will be shown in print, ensure main information remains visible; do not refer to color in captions for print versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit color illustrations as RGB (8 bits per channel). Check xerographic copy to see distinctions in black-and-white.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure lettering font, size, and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Helvetica or Arial (sans serif) for figure lettering. Keep lettering consistently sized (about 2–3 mm, 8–12 pt). Variance of type size within an illustration should be minimal; avoid effects like shading or outline letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include titles or captions within illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering and parts notation
rubrics_metrics.description: All figures are to be numbered using Arabic numerals and cited in text in consecutive order. Figure parts should be denoted by lowercase letters (a, b, c, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an appendix appears in the article and it contains figures, continue consecutive numbering of main text; do not use 'A1, A2' etc. Figures in online appendices (SI) should be numbered separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure captions format and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure should have a concise caption describing accurately what the figure depicts. Captions begin with the term 'Fig.' in bold followed by the figure number in bold, with no punctuation after the number and no punctuation at end of the caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include captions in the text file, not the figure file. Identify all elements found in the figure and identify previously published material by giving the original source at the end of the caption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure placement and sizing for column widths
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be submitted within the body of the text; size figures to fit column width. For large-sized journals: 84 mm (double-column) or 174 mm (single-column) wide and not higher than 234 mm. For small-sized journals: 119 mm wide and not higher than 195 mm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If file size causes upload problems, submit large figures separately from the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure accessibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure figures are accessible: provide descriptive captions, use patterns instead of or in addition to colors, and ensure any figure lettering has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures enable blind users and colorblind users to access content (text-to-speech, Braille).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI images policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must check Springer's policy on generative AI images and ensure work adheres to the described principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid undeclared or inappropriate use; verify compliance with publisher policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Information (SI) accepted formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer accepts electronic multimedia files (animations, movies, audio) and other supplementary files (e.g., .pdb, .wrl, .nb, .tex) to be published online along with an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submitting research datasets as SI, read the journal’s Research Data Policy. Encourage archiving data in repositories wherever possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary files submission details
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply all supplementary material in standard file formats and include in each file: article title, journal name, author names, affiliation and e-mail of corresponding author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep file sizes reasonable for download; larger files may require long download times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary audio/video technical constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspect ratio: 16:9 or 4:3; Maximum file size: 2 GB; Minimum video duration: 1 sec; Supported formats include avi, wmv, mp4, mov, m2p, mp2, mpg, mpeg, flv, mxf, mts, m4v, 3gp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure multimedia files meet these constraints to be accepted as SI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary text/presentation/spreadsheet formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit text and presentations as PDF; .doc or .ppt files are not suitable for long-term viability. Spreadsheets should be submitted as .csv or .xlsx.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A collection of figures may be combined in a PDF. Specialized formats are also acceptable where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary file naming, numbering and captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Number supplementary materials consecutively and refer to them as 'Online Resource' in the text (e.g., Online Resource 3). Name files consecutively (e.g., ESM_3.mpg, ESM_4.pdf) and supply a concise caption for each supplementary material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing: SI will be published as received from the author without conversion, editing, or reformatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility for supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide descriptive captions for each supplementary material; video files must not contain anything that flashes more than three times per second.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These steps help users with disabilities and reduce seizure risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-acceptance copyright and rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors will be asked to transfer copyright of the article to the Publisher (or grant exclusive publication and dissemination rights) to ensure protection and dissemination under copyright laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open Choice (OA) options preserve author copyright under a Creative Commons license instead of transferring copyright.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading limits and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofs are provided to check for typesetting or conversion errors and completeness/accuracy of text, tables and figures. Substantial changes in content (new results, corrected values, title, authorship) are not allowed without Editor approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After online publication, further changes can only be made by Erratum hyperlinked to the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online First publication and citation
rubrics_metrics.description: The article will be published online after corrected proofs and is the official first publication citable with the DOI; after print release, the paper can be cited by issue and page numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online First is the citable version for early dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Choice (hybrid Open Access) options and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Choice allows open access publication in Springer Nature journals; APCs vary by journal. Benefits include increased engagement, higher visibility and easier funder mandate compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open Choice articles are published under a Creative Commons license and do not require copyright transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Data Policy (type 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: This journal operates a type 1 research data policy: the journal encourages authors, where possible and applicable, to deposit data supporting findings in a public repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Datasets with DOIs may be cited in the reference list; data citations should include minimum DataCite information (authors, title, publisher repository, identifier). For double-blind review, consider blinding authorship in data access links.

rubrics_metrics.name: MSC classification code requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an appropriate number of MSC (Mathematics Subject Classification) codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MSC is used to categorize items for Mathematical Reviews and Zentralblatt MATH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific style for units and notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use internationally accepted signs and symbols for units (SI units). Use standard mathematical notation: italic for single letters denoting variables/constants; Roman/upright for numerals, operators, punctuation, and commonly defined functions (cos, det, e, exp, lim, log, max, min, sin, tan, d); bold for vectors, tensors, matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow discipline conventions for notation to ensure clarity and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical responsibilities and COPE adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal is committed to integrity and follows COPE guidelines to deal with misconduct. Authors should refrain from misrepresenting research results and follow good scientific practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines include originality, no simultaneous submission, avoiding salami-slicing, honest presentation of results, avoiding plagiarism (including text recycling), permissions for software/questionnaires, proper citation, and identification of potentially dual-use research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data/documentation for verification upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request authors should be prepared to send relevant documentation or data to verify the validity of results (raw data, samples, records), excluding sensitive confidential/proprietary data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain organized records and permissions to enable validation during peer review or after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of suspected misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: If misconduct is suspected, the Journal/Publisher will investigate per COPE; possible outcomes include rejection, erratum/correction, expression of concern, or retraction. The author’s institution may be informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction means article remains on platform, watermarked 'retracted' and explanation is provided. A notice of suspected transgression may be included in bibliographic records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to correct fundamental errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors have an obligation to correct mistakes once they discover a significant error or inaccuracy in their published article and must contact the journal to explain the impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision on correction or retraction depends on nature of error; retraction notes should provide transparency about impacted parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting or excluding reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may suggest suitable reviewers and/or request exclusion of certain individuals. Suggested reviewers must be totally independent and not connected to the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend a mix of reviewers from different countries and institutions. Provide institutional email for each suggested reviewer or alternative verification (homepage, publication record, researcher ID). The journal may not use suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Ethical Standards section
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should include information regarding sources of funding, potential conflicts of interest (financial or non-financial), informed consent (if human participants involved), and a statement on welfare of animals (if animals involved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards may vary by journal and article type. The corresponding author should be prepared to collect documentation of compliance and send if requested. Editors may reject manuscripts failing to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests disclosure timeframe and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are requested to disclose interests directly or indirectly related to the work, generally within the last 3 years of beginning the work; interests outside 3 years must be disclosed if they could reasonably be perceived as influencing the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding, employment, financial interests (stocks, consultancies, patents), and non-financial interests (positions, advisory roles, mentoring). Examples and sample wording are provided in guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of declarations and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Place summary of funding, competing interests, ethics approval, consent, data/material/code availability and authors' contribution statements in a 'Declarations' section before the reference list under headings such as 'Funding' and/or 'Competing interests'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When all authors have same/no conflicts, a single blanket statement is sufficient. See examples for formulations for funded, unfunded, and 'no competing interests' cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria and good practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended authorship criteria: authors listed must (1) have made substantial contributions to conception/design, acquisition/analysis/interpretation, or creation of new software; (2) drafted or revised work critically; (3) approved version to be published; (4) agree to be accountable for all aspects of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These guidelines are adapted from ICMJE and related recommendations. Publisher does not prescribe exact contribution types but recommends adherence to field-specific guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures and declarations expected from all authors
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors are requested to include information regarding funding sources, financial or non-financial interests, study-specific ethics approvals, informed consent, and animal welfare statements as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions about inclusion depend on journal scope and article type; work with public-health implications should include appropriate disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and responsibilities of the Corresponding Author
rubrics_metrics.description: One author is assigned as Corresponding Author to act on behalf of all co-authors and ensure questions related to accuracy/integrity are addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include ensuring all listed authors have approved the manuscript, managing communication between the journal and co-authors (may be delegated to Contact or Submitting Author), providing transparency on re-use/unpublished material, and ensuring disclosures and data statements from all authors are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author contributions statements and CRediT taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Publisher recommends including contribution statements specifying each author's contribution, either as free text or using the CRediT taxonomy (Conceptualization, Methodology, Formal analysis, Writing roles, Funding acquisition, Resources, Supervision, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For review articles where discrete contributions are less applicable, state who had the idea, who performed literature search and analysis, and who drafted/revised. For thesis-based articles, student is usually principal author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation and address rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary affiliation for each author should be the institution where the majority of their work was done. If an author has moved, the current address may additionally be stated. Addresses will not be updated after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure author names are present and spelled correctly; changes will not be made post-acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to authorship policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly advised to ensure correct author group, corresponding author, and order at submission. Changes to authorship are not accepted after acceptance. Adding/deleting authors at revision stage are generally not permitted but may be warranted with explanation and Editor-in-Chief approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval of authorship changes during revision is at the Editor-in-Chief's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author identification and ORCID recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are recommended to use their ORCID ID when submitting or acquire an ORCID via submission process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORCID use helps uniquely identify authors and link their contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deceased or incapacitated authors guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a co-author dies or is incapacitated during writing/submission/review and co-authors wish to include them, co-authors should obtain approval from a legal representative (e.g., direct relative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow appropriate legal/ethical procedures when including incapacitated/deceased authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship disputes resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of an authorship dispute during peer review or after acceptance/publication, the Journal will not adjudicate and authors should resolve the dispute themselves; if unable, the Journal reserves the right to withdraw a manuscript or raise the issue with authors’ institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should attempt institutional resolution; the journal may involve institutions if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should treat all communication with the Journal as confidential, including correspondence with Editors and reviewers’ reports, unless explicit consent to share has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain confidentiality to protect peer review integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of editing services
rubrics_metrics.description: Using Springer Nature Author Services (English editing, developmental comments, formatting, figure preparation, translation) is optional and not required for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using such services does not guarantee acceptance or selection for peer review. A free Grammar Check tool is available.
